text:
alex: Heads-up — after today's console deploy some Editor users report they can't rotate team API keys. UI shows the button but action fails with 403. No audit entry for the attempt.
maria: repro steps? can you paste exact flow / API call
alex: Steps: 1) Console > Teams > select team > Keys tab 2) Click Rotate key 3) Spinner -> toast "permission denied"
alex: curl.simplified example we hit from UI (from browser devtools):\n```\nPOST /api/v1/teams/tn_123/keys/rotate HTTP/1.1\nAuthorization: Bearer <user-token>\nContent-Type: application/json\n{ "key_id": "k_abc" }\n```
ken: I think this ties to the KMS permission-change PR merged this morning (https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/842). That PR hardened the kms:Encrypt permission check and added an extra required scope for non-admins.
samir: I see ~30 failed rotates in Sentry since 10:05am with 403 and message "missing kms:encrypt scope". stack trace shows check at auth/service.go:212
auditor-bot: Audit log notice: no entries created for rotate-key endpoints because the audit middleware short-circuits on auth failure. Missing logs for both success and failure is a compliance issue.
julie: Customer impact? any paying accounts affected?
alex: Affected are users in Editor role across several small customers (3 orgs reported). No Dedicated/Private customers yet. They can't rotate keys which blocks key rotation workflows.
maria: Quick triage idea — if the KMS change accidentally required kms:encrypt on the *user* token instead of service principal, Editors without the new scope would 403. Can we confirm who the auth check expects? ken: yes, it now checks principal.Scope.Contains("kms:encrypt") before allowing rotate. That should have checked the service role on the backend, not the end-user token.
ken: Proposed mitigation: revert the scope change or short-circuit to allow rotate for Editors while we patch. Revert is fastest to restore from-prod behavior.
maria: Also need to add audit entries even on auth failures — that's req by compliance (SOX internal policy). We'll add middleware to log attempted actions with masked payload.
samir: I can push a temporary ACL bypass for rotate-key to unblock customers, but I'd prefer a revert and fix to auth logic. Bypass increases attack surface.
julie: Suggest severity P2 (customer-facing but limited). Notify support and affected accounts. PR cadence: revert hotfix now, then follow-up patch, tests, and add audit fix.
oncall-bot: Incident channel created: #inc-1852201123-key-rotate-regression
alex: I'll notify support and paste affected org IDs in the channel. Also tagging CS to reach out.
ken: I'm opening hotfix revert PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/1912. Patch details: revert kms scope gate in auth/service.go, add TODO comment and ticket link. Test: manual rotate on staging + unit for principal resolution.
ken: Follow-up ticket to rework check: INFRA-1297 — validate using service principal for KMS ops + audit-on-failure. Will add e2e that simulates Editor role.
maria: I'll pick up the audit middleware change (AUD-434). Plan: log action "team.rotate_key_attempt" with result "denied" and masked key_id.
alex: We should also add a canary deploy for the proper fix to Dedicated region before wide rollout.
samir: Monitoring: I'll add an alert for spike in rotate_key 403s and missing-audit-rate threshold.
julie: Communication: draft email to affected customers + postmortem to be ready within 72h. For now we say: temporary regression fixed, fix rolling out, no evidence of key leakage.
alex: thanks all — will follow-up in #inc-1852201123-key-rotate-regression with updates and customer list.
